fact: Equatorial Guinea's government decided on 2026-09-09 that all Starlink sales go through the regulator ORTEL (legal selling authority under the State Secretariat for Artificial Intelligence) and that contracts bought outside official channels be cancelled; the outlet (Tech.Africa) says the service has not formally launched and no price or date was given.

Vice-president Nguema Obiang Mangue announced on 2026-09-09 that Equatorial Guinea officially launched Starlink satellite internet, operated by SpaceX, with sale and distribution centralised and requests handled by ORTEL; earlier connections made with foreign details are to be deactivated.

A 2026-09-09 government session praised the Transport Ministry's agreement with Starlink to market satellite internet in Equatorial Guinea, placed legal selling authority with ORTEL, ordered individuals' contracts outside official channels cancelled, and noted oil companies are already authorised to use the network offshore.

Elon Musk and Starlink's official X accounts announced on 2026-08-29 that Starlink service is now available in Equatorial Guinea, shown as available on the company coverage map (company announcement as reported by Revista Real EG).

In July 2026 the government temporarily authorised US offshore oil companies to use Starlink, by a document signed by the Minister of State for Transport, Telecommunications and Civil Aviation (offshore corporate use, temporary authorisation).

At a 2026-07-28 meeting the Vice-President was told Starlink's type-approval with regulator ORTEL was still pending with competences undefined and ordered ORTEL to speed it up; the first phase is for public bodies, airport terminals and selected companies only, with extension to private users conditional on negotiations and justified on security grounds.

Government release says the Transport Ministry reached an agreement with Starlink to sell satellite internet in the country, and the Vice-President directed that legal authority to sell rests with state operator ORTEL under the Secretariat of State for AI; oil companies were already authorised to use the network offshore.

The Vice-President announced on 8 September 2026 that Starlink satellite internet is officially available nationwide after a service agreement with Starlink, with new requests centralised by regulator Ortel; this widened a restricted authorisation for North American offshore oil firms (dated 29 July by this outlet).
Starlink launched under a provisional approval granted by the Vice-President on 29 July 2026 (as dated by this document), with GITGE assessing operations and long-term conditions.

Starlink went live on 29 August 2026, confirmed by Starlink and Elon Musk, with an order page on starlink.com and two residential tiers priced in FCFA; sold directly by Starlink under provisional approval.
